Help me implement an interview assignment due in three days. Prioritize a simple, runnable project that I can understand and explain—not an elaborate production platform.

Assignment:
Build a multi-agent production incident investigation system with these six roles:
Orchestrator, Observability, Dependency, Reasoning, Critic, and Reporting.

It must investigate simulated logs, metrics, deployment/configuration history, service dependencies, and historical incidents. Evidence can be incomplete or misleading. Agents must exchange structured results and collaborate through targeted follow-up investigations, not merely form a fixed prompt chain.

Requirements:

- Parallel independent investigations.
- Shared state and explicit task dependencies.
- Critic-driven feedback loops.
- Bounded retries, execution budgets, and failure recovery.
- Reports with ranked hypotheses, supporting/contradicting evidence, confidence, assumptions, recommended actions, and an inconclusive option.
- At least 10 synthetic incidents and automated tests.
- Comparison against an iterative single-agent baseline using the same tools.
- Metrics: root-cause accuracy, evidence grounding, tool calls, latency, and token consumption.
- Setup instructions, architecture diagram, evaluation results, and a technical note of at most 500 words.
- I must submit my actual coding-assistant transcript.

Use Python, asyncio, Pydantic, pytest, and one LLM provider SDK. Avoid LangChain/LangGraph, databases, vector search, web APIs, Docker, and a frontend unless genuinely necessary. Use local JSON files for synthetic data.

Keep the project small. A sensible starting layout is:

- models.py: typed contracts
- tools.py: simulated tools and failure injection
- agents.py: six agent roles
- investigation.py: state and orchestration
- baseline.py: single-agent investigation
- llm.py: one provider adapter
- evaluate.py and cli.py
- data/ and tests/

Adjust this only when a clear need arises. Do not create empty abstractions.

For this stage:

1. Inspect the existing workspace and preserve unrelated work.
2. Briefly explain the design and implementation stages.
3. Implement the typed contracts, shared investigation state, five tool families, and 10 synthetic incidents.
4. Add focused tests for tools and data integrity.
5. Make the foundation runnable without an API key.

Tools must return structured complete, partial, or error results. Preserve source, query, time range, and coverage metadata. Tool failures must never look like successful empty results.

Include incidents covering straightforward causes, a misleading deployment, conflicting observations, misleading historical similarity, incomplete data, transient tool failure, and an intentionally inconclusive case. Cases may combine challenges.

Keep evaluator ground truth separate from agent-visible data. Do not expose diagnostic labels through filenames, scenario titles, tool metadata, or incident IDs. Do not implement case-specific answer logic.

Ask me about my LLM provider before implementing the live adapter. Never ask me to paste credentials into chat.

Stop after this foundation is implemented and its tests run. Explain what exists, important decisions, and what remains. Do not claim that the full assignment is complete.

It does not diagnose incidents,\n+call an LLM, or generate final investigation reports.\n+\n+## Setup\n+\n+Requires Python 3.11 or newer. Never put credentials in\n+chat; a later adapter will use environment variables.\n+\n+## Files and design\n+\n+| File | Responsibility |\n+| --- | --- |\n+| `models.py` | Pydantic contracts for six roles, records, tool results, coverage, tasks, structured agent exchanges, ranked/inconclusive reports, and budgets |\n+| `tools.py` | One uniform async query interface over five typed local tool families |\n+| `investigation.py` | Shared evidence ledger, task dependencies, budget accounting, and bounded tool-task execution |\n+| `cli.py` | Offline parallel evidence collector and JSON snapshot output |\n+| `data/incidents.json` | Ten incidents with neutral IDs and symptom-only alerts; the only investigation dataset |\n+| `data/simulation.json` | Runtime-only latency/failure settings, not returned in tool results |\n+| `data/evaluation/ground_truth.json` | Evaluator-only answers and challenge tags; never loaded by runtime code |\n+| `tests/` | Data integrity, provenance, coverage, filters, failures, shared state, and concurrent execution |\n+\n+```mermaid\n+flowchart TD\n+    CLI[Offline CLI collector] --> S[Shared investigation state]\n+    S --> D[Dependency gates and ready tasks]\n+    D --> B[Global budgets / semaphore / bounded retries]\n+    B --> P{Concurrent independent tool queries}\n+    P --> L[Logs]\n+    P --> M[Metrics]\n+    P --> C[Deployment and configuration history]\n+    P --> G[Service dependencies]\n+    P --> H[Historical incidents]\n+    V[Agent-visible incidents.json] --> P\n+    F[Runtime simulation.json] --> B\n+    L --> R[Typed complete / partial / error results]\n+    M --> R\n+    C --> R\n+    G --> R\n+    H --> R\n+    R --> E[Evidence ledger + per-task attempt provenance]\n+    E --> S\n+    S --> O[Structured offline snapshot]\n+    T[Evaluator-only ground_truth.json] -. future evaluator only .-> EV[Evaluation - not implemented]\n+```\n+\n+### Tool semantics\n+\n+`ToolQuery` contains an incident ID, family, timezone-aware time range, optional\n+service filter, and result limit. All time windows are half-open `[start, end)`.\n+Services filter the emitting/calling service, including dependency edges.\n+An empty filter means all services covered by that source, **not** all services in\n+the system. To check a missing service, request it explicitly.\n+\n+Historical records use the timestamp of the past incident; query a lookback\n+window to retrieve them. The CLI uses 90 days. All other records represent\n+timestamped events or samples, including dependency observations. Coverage denotes\n+the retained source interval, not a promise of continuous measurement or complete\n+knowledge of every dependency. Unknown dependency health is an observation, not\n+proof that the dependency was healthy.\n+\n+Every result retains source, original query, collection time, observed intervals,\n+gaps, service coverage, matched/returned counts, and truncation. Returned records\n+have stable evidence IDs. A fully covered query with no matches is `complete`\n+and empty; a missing interval/service or truncation is `partial` with explicit\n+issues. A tool failure is `error`, has a code/message/retryability, and cannot\n+claim observed evidence. Failed attempts remain in state after a successful retry.\n+\n+Tools are read-only: no external services and no mutations to incident data.\n+Failure injection applies to the first N calls for an incident/family in a tool\n+instance; `failures: null` injects persistent failure. A fresh instance resets\n+failure counters. Future multi-agent/baseline comparisons must each use a fresh\n+instance with identical settings and budgets.\n+\n+### Shared state and limits\n+\n+Tasks have explicit dependencies, an assigned role, and at most five attempts\n+(two by default). Registration rejects missing dependencies and cycles atomically.\n+Failed prerequisites block dependents; independent work can continue.\n+The CLI registers five independent tool tasks with no artificial dependencies.\n+The six roles are contracts only; no agent role is implemented yet.\n+\n+Default limits are 30 total tool calls, 30 seconds, 2 seconds per tool call,\n+five parallel tools, and a 20,000-token reservation budget. Retries and timed-out\n+calls count toward the global call budget; time spent waiting for a parallel slot\n+counts toward the deadline. Local simulated retries need no backoff.\n+API-free runs consume zero LLM tokens. The token hook currently tracks conservative\n+reservations, not provider-measured consumption; actual input/output usage accounting\n+must be added with the adapter.\n+\n+Structured findings, hypotheses, and targeted follow-up requests can be stored\n+with validated evidence references. Publishing a result does **not** automatically\n+schedule its follow-ups; the future orchestrator must decide and register them.\n+Evidence reference validation checks existence, not whether a claim is logically\n+entailed. That distinction matters for the future grounding metric and Critic.\n+\n+The data covers straightforward causes, misleading deployments/history, scoped\n+conflicting observations, missing data, transient failure, and insufficient evidence.\n+Challenge labels exist only in the evaluator file. This is a separation of runtime\n+inputs, **not** an OS-level security boundary; agents must receive tool results and\n+never arbitrary filesystem access to evaluator data. There is no case-specific\n+answer logic.\n+\n+## Remaining implementation stages\n+\n+1. Choose an LLM provider before adding its single SDK and `llm.py`. Implement\n+   structured responses, bounded model calls, and actual token usage accounting.\n+2. Add the six role implementations and dynamic orchestration: independent initial\n+   investigations, Reasoning hypotheses, Critic-triggered targeted follow-ups,\n+   explicit dependencies, and bounded rounds. Reporting must allow inconclusive\n+   outcomes and distinguish evidence from assumptions.\n+3. Add an iterative single-agent baseline using exactly the same tools, inputs,\n+   and budgets. Evaluate both on all ten cases; record root-cause accuracy,\n+   evidence grounding, tool calls, latency, and token consumption. Add agent and\n+   orchestration tests and measured evaluation results.\n+4. Finalize the architecture diagram and a technical note of at most 500 words.\n+   Export and submit the **actual coding-assistant transcript**, including this\n+   foundation work and later changes. No reconstructed transcript is supplied.\n+\n+## Technical note (foundation only; under 500 words)\n+\n+The foundation separates observations from conclusions. Five async tool families\n+share one query envelope while returning typed records. Each response preserves\n+source, time and service coverage, truncation, and explicit error details. Empty\n+evidence is meaningful only when the requested source scope was observed. Partial\n+coverage never becomes a successful empty fallback.\n+\n+Shared state centralizes stable evidence IDs, per-task attempts, dependencies, and\n+execution budgets. Dependency graphs are validated before registration. Global\n+call reservations are atomic across concurrent tasks. Retries, per-call timeouts,\n+and the overall deadline are bounded. Failed prerequisites block downstream work\n+without blocking independent investigations. No LLM is required to exercise these\n+mechanisms.\n+\n+The ten cases use neutral identifiers and operational alerts. Historical incidents\n+may resemble current symptoms without sharing their cause. Scoped observations may\n+appear contradictory. Missing data is declared through coverage rather than hidden\n+in empty lists. One case intentionally lacks a defensible root cause. Ground truth\n+is stored separately and is unavailable through the simulated tool interface.\n+\n+The collector is not a multi-agent system or a diagnostic baseline. Role outputs,\n+follow-up requests, and report contracts are defined, but model-backed collaboration\n+is deliberately deferred. The next stage must connect Critic feedback to targeted\n+tasks rather than run a fixed prompt chain, then measure both systems fairly using\n+identical tools and budgets. Token reservations are not a substitute for actual\n+provider usage measurements. Evaluation results and the final technical note remain\n+to be completed with the real agent implementation.\n*** End Patch\n",

C:\\Users\\akkulkarni\\.copilot\\chats\\2026-11-07\\ideal-carnival-8c17e37b\\README.md\n+# Incident investigation: offline foundation\n+\n+This is **stage 1**, not the completed multi-agent assignment. It collects local\n+synthetic evidence concurrently without an API key. It does not diagnose incidents,\n+call an LLM, or generate final investigation reports.\n+\n+## Setup\n+\n+Requires Python 3.11 or newer. From this directory in PowerShell:\n+\n+```powershell\n+python -m venv .venv\n+.\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe -m pip install -e \".[dev]\"\n+.\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe cli.py list\n+.\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe cli.py collect inc-007\n+.\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe cli.py collect inc-006 --json\n+.\\.venv\\Scripts\\python.exe -m pytest\n+```\n+\n+On macOS/Linux use `.venv/bin/python` instead. No activation is necessary.\n+Run from the source checkout; editable installation leaves JSON fixtures beside\n+the modules. Distributing a wheel with bundled fixtures is outside this stage.\n+No provider SDK is installed until a provider is chosen. Never put credentials in\n+chat; a later adapter will use environment variables.\n+\n+## Files and design\n+\n+| File | Responsibility |\n+| --- | --- |\n+| `models.py` | Pydantic contracts for six roles, records, tool results, coverage, tasks, structured agent exchanges, ranked/inconclusive reports, and budgets |\n+| `tools.py` | One uniform async query interface over five typed local tool families |\n+| `investigation.py` | Shared evidence ledger, task dependencies, budget accounting, and bounded tool-task execution |\n+| `cli.py` | Offline parallel evidence collector and JSON snapshot output |\n+| `data/incidents.json` | Ten incidents with neutral IDs and symptom-only alerts; the only investigation dataset |\n+| `data/simulation.json` | Runtime-only latency/failure settings, not returned in tool results |\n+| `data/evaluation/ground_truth.json` | Evaluator-only answers and challenge tags; never loaded by runtime code |\n+| `tests/` | Data integrity, provenance, coverage, filters, failures, shared state, and concurrent execution |\n+\n+```mermaid\n+flowchart TD\n+    CLI[Offline CLI collector] --> S[Shared investigation state]\n+    S --> D[Dependency gates and ready tasks]\n+    D --> B[Global budgets / semaphore / bounded retries]\n+    B --> P{Concurrent independent tool queries}\n+    P --> L[Logs]\n+    P --> M[Metrics]\n+    P --> C[Deployment and configuration history]\n+    P --> G[Service dependencies]\n+    P --> H[Historical incidents]\n+    V[Agent-visible incidents.json] --> P\n+    F[Runtime simulation.json] --> B\n+    L --> R[Typed complete / partial / error results]\n+    M --> R\n+    C --> R\n+    G --> R\n+    H --> R\n+    R --> E[Evidence ledger + per-task attempt provenance]\n+    E --> S\n+    S --> O[Structured offline snapshot]\n+    T[Evaluator-only ground_truth.json] -. future evaluator only .-> EV[Evaluation - not implemented]\n+```\n+\n+### Tool semantics\n+\n+`ToolQuery` contains an incident ID, family, timezone-aware time range, optional\n+service filter, and result limit. All time windows are half-open `[start, end)`.\n+Services filter the emitting/calling service, including dependency edges.\n+An empty filter means all services covered by that source, **not** all services in\n+the system. To check a missing service, request it explicitly.\n+\n+Historical records use the timestamp of the past incident; query a lookback\n+window to retrieve them. The CLI uses 90 days. All other records represent\n+timestamped events or samples, including dependency observations. Coverage denotes\n+the retained source interval, not a promise of continuous measurement or complete\n+knowledge of every dependency. Unknown dependency health is an observation, not\n+proof that the dependency was healthy.\n+\n+Every result retains source, original query, collection time, observed intervals,\n+gaps, service coverage, matched/returned counts, and truncation. Returned records\n+have stable evidence IDs. A fully covered query with no matches is `complete`\n+and empty; a missing interval/service or truncation is `partial` with explicit\n+issues. A tool failure is `error`, has a code/message/retryability, and cannot\n+claim observed evidence. Failed attempts remain in state after a successful retry.\n+\n+Tools are read-only: no external services and no mutations to incident data.\n+Failure injection applies to the first N calls for an incident/family in a tool\n+instance; `failures: null` injects persistent failure. A fresh instance resets\n+failure counters. Future multi-agent/baseline comparisons must each use a fresh\n+instance with identical settings and budgets.\n+\n+### Shared state and limits\n+\n+Tasks have explicit dependencies, an assigned role, and at most five attempts\n+(two by default). Registration rejects missing dependencies and cycles atomically.\n+Failed prerequisites block dependents; independent work can continue.\n+The CLI registers five independent tool tasks with no artificial dependencies.\n+The six roles are contracts only; no agent role is implemented yet.\n+\n+Default limits are 30 total tool calls, 30 seconds, 2 seconds per tool call,\n+five parallel tools, and a 20,000-token reservation budget. Retries and timed-out\n+calls count toward the global call budget; time spent waiting for a parallel slot\n+counts toward the deadline. Local simulated retries need no backoff.\n+API-free runs consume zero LLM tokens. The token hook currently tracks conservative\n+reservations, not provider-measured consumption; actual input/output usage accounting\n+must be added with the adapter.\n+\n+Structured findings, hypotheses, and targeted follow-up requests can be stored\n+with validated evidence references. Publishing a result does **not** automatically\n+schedule its follow-ups; the future orchestrator must decide and register them.\n+Evidence reference validation checks existence, not whether a claim is logically\n+entailed. That distinction matters for the future grounding metric and Critic.\n+\n+The data covers straightforward causes, misleading deployments/history, scoped\n+conflicting observations, missing data, transient failure, and insufficient evidence.\n+Challenge labels exist only in the evaluator file. This is a separation of runtime\n+inputs, **not** an OS-level security boundary; agents must receive tool results and\n+never arbitrary filesystem access to evaluator data. There is no case-specific\n+answer logic.\n+\n+## Remaining implementation stages\n+\n+1. Choose an LLM provider before adding its single SDK and `llm.py`. Implement\n+   structured responses, bounded model calls, and actual token usage accounting.\n+2. Add the six role implementations and dynamic orchestration: independent initial\n+   investigations, Reasoning hypotheses, Critic-triggered targeted follow-ups,\n+   explicit dependencies, and bounded rounds. Reporting must allow inconclusive\n+   outcomes and distinguish evidence from assumptions.\n+3. Add an iterative single-agent baseline using exactly the same tools, inputs,\n+   and budgets. Five async tool families\n+share one query envelope while returning typed records. Each response preserves\n+source, time and service coverage, truncation, and explicit error details. Empty\n+evidence is meaningful only when the requested source scope was observed. Partial\n+coverage never becomes a successful empty fallback.\n+\n+Shared state centralizes stable evidence IDs, per-task attempts, dependencies, and\n+execution budgets. Dependency graphs are validated before registration. Global\n+call reservations are atomic across concurrent tasks. Retries, per-call timeouts,\n+and the overall deadline are bounded. Failed prerequisites block downstream work\n+without blocking independent investigations. No LLM is required to exercise these\n+mechanisms.\n+\n+The ten cases use neutral identifiers and operational alerts. Historical incidents\n+may resemble current symptoms without sharing their cause. Scoped observations may\n+appear contradictory. Missing data is declared through coverage rather than hidden\n+in empty lists. One case intentionally lacks a defensible root cause. Ground truth\n+is stored separately and is unavailable through the simulated tool interface.\n+\n+The collector is not a multi-agent system or a diagnostic baseline. Role outputs,\n+follow-up requests, and report contracts are defined, but model-backed collaboration\n+is deliberately deferred. The next stage must connect Critic feedback to targeted\n+tasks rather than run a fixed prompt chain, then measure both systems fairly using\n+identical tools and budgets. Continue from the existing foundation. Implement a working multi-agent investigation and an iterative single-agent baseline. Keep the design simple and reuse the existing contracts and tools.

Implement all six roles:
- Orchestrator: plans evidence tasks, schedules them, and decides whether to continue.
- Observability: investigates logs and metrics.
- Dependency: investigates deployments/configuration, dependencies, and historical incidents.
- Reasoning: compares competing hypotheses using evidence.
- Critic: challenges unsupported claims and requests discriminating evidence.
- Reporting: produces the final structured report without adding new evidence.

Use the agreed LLM provider. All roles can share one model and client. Use validated structured model responses rather than parsing arbitrary prose. Keep prompts readable.

The runtime—not the LLM—must enforce tool access, schemas, dependencies, budgets, and retries.

Required collaboration:
1. Orchestrator creates an initial task plan.
2. Independent Observability and Dependency tasks execute concurrently.
3. Their structured results enter a shared evidence ledger.
4. Reasoning proposes and compares plausible hypotheses.
5. Critic returns specific objections and targeted follow-up requests.
6. Orchestrator schedules valid follow-ups.
7. Reasoning revises hypotheses using new evidence.
8. Reporting produces a grounded or inconclusive result.

A fixed sequence that always performs the same follow-up is insufficient. Follow-ups must respond to evidence gaps, and duplicate queries should be avoided unless intentionally retrying a failure.

Use a small task model with IDs, dependencies, statuses, and outputs. Serialize state updates through the coordinator to avoid races.

Use sensible documented defaults, such as:
- Two follow-up rounds maximum.
- Three total attempts per transiently failing operation.
- Explicit total tool, LLM/token, and wall-clock budgets.

Record failures and termination reasons. Retry only eligible failures. If critical analysis or evidence remains unavailable, report the limitation rather than returning an ordinary success.

Implement the baseline as one LLM agent that can repeatedly choose tools, inspect results, revise hypotheses, and finish. Give it the same visible data, tools, model, report schema, and total resource ceilings as the multi-agent system.

Provide CLI commands for running either approach on an incident and saving the report and execution trace.

Use mocked LLM responses for automated tests, including a test where Critic feedback causes a new query and a hypothesis revision. Clearly distinguish mocked execution from real model reasoning.

Run relevant tests. If credentials are unavailable, complete the implementation and offline tests, but state that live execution is unverified. Ask before starting paid LLM runs.

Authentication, refusal, incomplete output,\n+invalid schemas/references/access and exhausted budgets are not retryable. Model\n+retry waits are bounded; local fixture tools need no backoff. Failed prerequisites\n+block dependents. Missing scripts fail preflight; none\n+are silently invented. Mocked batches identify `scripted-test-double`, store null\n+provider token measurements, and label summaries **plumbing only, not LLM performance**.\n+There is no LLM judge and no fabricated all-incident prediction script.\n+\n+Use a **new output directory** for every batch. Outputs are:\n+`manifest.json`, `results.json`, `results.csv`, `summary.md`, and individual\n+`runs\\INCIDENT.APPROACH.REPETITION\\report.json` / `trace.json`.\n+`runs.jsonl` journals completed rows, including failures, so interrupted batches\n+retain completed work. A partial batch has no completed comparison summary;\n+automatic resume/merging is intentionally not implemented.\n+\n+The manifest captures the full planned order, selected incidents, repeats, shared\n+model settings/budget, Python/dependency versions, implementation/data/rubric hashes\n+and failure-policy version. Pair order alternates across incidents/repetitions to\n+reduce systematic warm-up/order bias; runs are not executed as competing parallel\n+benchmarks. Provider caching/availability and model aliases can still vary.\n+Use a provider-pinned model identifier where available. Temperature 0 does not\n+guarantee identical provider responses or latency.\n+\n+## Deterministic, limited scoring rubric\n+\n+`data/evaluation/rubric.json` contains expected facts, bounded case-specific English\n+patterns (all required patterns must match; listed rejection patterns veto a match),\n+and curated positive/negative evidence relationships. All of it is evaluator-only.\n+Agents see only the **same generic category vocabulary for every incident**:\n+`connection_capacity`, `response_contract`, `upstream_availability`, `memory_capacity`,\n+`name_resolution`, `queue_delivery`, `logging_backpressure`, `tls_validation`,\n+`request_capacity`, and `unknown`. Categories alone never earn root-cause credit.\n+\n+| Metric | Definition and limits |\n+| --- | --- |\n+| Top-ranked root-cause accuracy | On answerable cases, a ranked top hypothesis must select the expected generic category and express all required distinguishing facts in its claim. Abstentions and terminal failures count as incorrect; every planned answerable row remains in the denominator. This is **rubric accuracy**, not arbitrary-prose semantic verification. |\n+| Abstention frequency | Explicit inconclusive reports divided by all runs. Missing reports from crashes are listed separately, not credited as intentional decisions. |\n+| Intentionally inconclusive handling | The inconclusive case must produce an inconclusive report with a recognized insufficiency explanation and no terminal execution/analysis failure. A provider-error fallback is abstention, but not correct analytical handling. |\n+| Citation existence | Fraction of cited IDs present in that incident's source corpus, counted once per hypothesis/polarity. |\n+| Citation availability | Fraction actually acquired into that run's ledger with matching source record content. Existing but uncollected IDs receive no availability credit. |\n+| Support-link precision | A support citation must be available and explicitly linked to a recognized fact in that hypothesis's claim. A normal-database metric or similar historical incident cannot support the current configuration/DNS diagnosis merely because its ID exists. |\n+| Counterevidence-link precision | Available contradicting citations must be listed as opposing a matched fact. Citing opposition as support earns no support credit. |\n+| Rubric fact support | Fraction of recognized facts with a complete allowed support witness set. Some facts require joint witnesses, e.g. queue timeout configuration plus job duration. Counterevidence does not establish the positive claim. |\n+| Tool calls | Runtime reservations/attempts, including retries/timeouts; checked against per-task attempt totals. No-dispatch budget errors add no tool call. |\n+| Latency | Measured from per-run preparation and runner entry through completion/failure, including all analyses, retries and waiting; excludes batch setup and output-file I/O. The outer deadline also bounds preparation plus execution. |\n+| Provider tokens | Sum reported input/output usage across every model call, including failed validation. Unknown calls retain reservation totals separately; measured subtotals are labeled incomplete. Mocked values are null, never real-provider zeros. |\n+| Failure/budget status | All transient, terminal, cancelled and exhausted outcomes are retained with errors, termination reason and trace. Missing counters are null rather than guessed. |\n+\n+No-citation/no-matched-fact rates are **null**, not perfect scores. Grounding\n+precision is conditional on emitted citations; failures with no citations still\n+appear in rows, failure rates, no-citation counts and the accuracy denominator.\n+Aggregate citation/fact denominators are saved. Resource means show measured\n+sample counts and missing values rather than silently pretending failed runs\n+used zero resources.\n+\n+This rubric is intentionally narrow: it can recognize only enumerated facts,\n+their listed witnesses and a few explicit negations. Novel paraphrases may be\n+missed, and extra assertions attached to a recognized fact may escape checking.\n+Unmatched claims are counted, **not proven false**; matched prose is not certified\n+fully entailed. Actions, assumptions and general causal reasoning are not scored.\n+Versioning the private rubric makes these limits auditable without claiming an\n+overly general semantic verifier. Wrong hypotheses can have valid citations but\n+poor support scores; correct guesses can have high accuracy and poor grounding.\n+\n+`results.json` retains per-run values, per-repetition aggregate rates, sample\n+standard deviations across repetitions, per-incident variability and resource\n+distributions. One observation has no standard-deviation estimate. Variability\n+across repetitions is distinct from variability across different incidents.\n+Failures are never dropped from the scheduled run grid.\n+\n ## Remaining assignment work\n@@\n-credits. A provider-error fallback is abstention, but not correct analytical handling. |\n+| Citation existence | Fraction of cited IDs present in that incident's source corpus, counted once per hypothesis/polarity. |\n+| Citation availability | Fraction actually acquired into that run's ledger with matching source record content. Existing but uncollected IDs receive no availability credit. |\n+| Support-link precision | A support citation must be available and explicitly linked to a recognized fact in that hypothesis's claim. A normal-database metric or similar historical incident cannot support the current configuration/DNS diagnosis merely because its ID exists. |\n+| Counterevidence-link precision | Available contradicting citations must be listed as opposing a matched fact. Citing opposition as support earns no support credit. |\n+| Rubric fact support | Fraction of recognized facts with a complete allowed support witness set. Some facts require joint witnesses, e.g. queue timeout configuration plus job duration. Counterevidence does not establish the positive claim. |\n+| Tool calls | Runtime reservations/attempts, including retries/timeouts; checked against per-task attempt totals. No-dispatch budget errors add no tool call. |\n+| Latency | Measured from per-run preparation and runner entry through completion/failure, including all analyses, retries and waiting; excludes batch setup and output-file I/O. The outer deadline also bounds preparation plus execution. |\n+| Provider tokens | Sum reported input/output usage across every model call, including failed validation. Unknown calls retain reservation totals separately; measured subtotals are labeled incomplete. Mocked values are null, never real-provider zeros. |\n+| Failure/budget status | All transient, terminal, cancelled and exhausted outcomes are retained with errors, termination reason and trace. Missing counters are null rather than guessed. |\n+\n+No-citation/no-matched-fact rates are **null**, not perfect scores. Grounding\n+precision is conditional on emitted citations; failures with no citations still\n+appear in rows, failure rates, no-citation counts and the accuracy denominator.\n+Aggregate citation/fact denominators are saved. Resource means show measured\n+sample counts and missing values rather than silently pretending failed runs\n+used zero resources.\n+\n+This rubric is intentionally narrow: it can recognize only enumerated facts,\n+their listed witnesses and a few explicit negations. Novel paraphrases may be\n+missed, and extra assertions attached to a recognized fact may escape checking.\n+Unmatched claims are counted, **not proven false**; matched prose is not certified\n+fully entailed. Actions, assumptions and general causal reasoning are not scored.\n+Versioning the private rubric makes these limits auditable without claiming an\n+overly general semantic verifier. Wrong hypotheses can have valid citations but\n+poor support scores; correct guesses can have high accuracy and poor grounding.\n+\n+`results.json` retains per-run values, per-repetition aggregate rates, sample\n+standard deviations across repetitions, per-incident variability and resource\n+distributions. One observation has no standard-deviation estimate. Variability\n+across repetitions is distinct from variability across different incidents.\n+Failures are never dropped from the scheduled run grid.\n+\n ## Remaining assignment work\n \n Live-run verification requires local credentials and explicit permission to spend\n-credits. The evaluator (`evaluate.py`), root-cause accuracy/semantic evidence\n-grounding metrics and measured multi-agent versus baseline results remain to be\n-implemented. Traces already retain tool calls, latency and provider token usage\n-needed for those comparisons. Export and submit the **actual coding-assistant\n-transcript**, including foundation and stage-2 work; do not reconstruct one.\n+credits. The harness and offline plumbing tests are implemented, but measured live\n+multi-agent versus baseline results and their interpretation remain outstanding.\n+Export and submit the **actual coding-assistant transcript**, including foundation,\n+agent implementation and evaluation work; do not reconstruct one.\n \n ## Technical note (under 500 words)\n \n@@ -250,7 +353,12 @@\n Historical resemblance and change timing are leads, not guaranteed causes.\n Mocked tests demonstrate concurrency, targeted Critic feedback, hypothesis revision,\n budget enforcement, recovery and persisted traces. They do not establish prediction\n-accuracy. Citation validation cannot prove semantic grounding; Critic judgments\n-still require evaluation. Live execution and measured comparative evaluation remain\n+accuracy. Citation validation cannot prove semantic grounding. The deterministic evaluator\n+uses private expected facts and witness sets to distinguish citation existence\n+from limited claim support, without a semantic judge. Categories are generic;\n+the per-incident answer mapping never enters prompts. Query-keyed failure counters\n+make injected errors independent of parallel scheduling. Paired repeated runs\n+share model settings and total ceilings, retain failures, and save JSON/CSV,\n+traces, manifests and variability. Live execution and measured comparative evaluation remain\n unverified, so the complete interview assignment is not yet finished.\n \n"

## 2026-11-07T09:20:22.194Z - assistant.message

Event ID: `cd3594a1-47b8-4fa4-90a8-f3885791a593`

**The evaluation harness is implemented; all 175 tests passed, including 26 evaluation tests.**

`evaluate.py` runs both approaches over the ten incidents with identical model settings, data, tools, and per-incident ceilings. Fresh tool instances use **query-keyed failure injection**, so scheduling order cannot consume another query’s failures.

The evaluator measures root-cause accuracy, abstention, inconclusive-case handling, tool calls, latency, provider tokens, and failure/budget status. Grounding separately checks **citation existence, acquisition, support relationships, and complete fact witness sets**. The private rubric is deliberately limited—not a general semantic verifier or LLM judge.

Each batch writes `results.json`, `results.csv`, `summary.md`, a reproducibility manifest, and per-run reports/traces. Repeated runs include variability estimates; failures and unknown measurements remain explicit.

`README.md` documents commands and scoring limits. **No paid runs were made, and no live benchmark results exist.** Mocked execution is labeled plumbing-only; live execution remains gated by `--allow-paid`.

\"citation_count\": 0, \"existing_citations\": 0, \"available_citations\": 0,\n         \"supporting_citation_count\": 0, \"support_relationship_matches\": 0,\n }\n     for hypothesis in run.report.hypotheses:\n         facts = [fact for fact in rubric.facts if fact.matches(hypothesis.claim)]\n         counts[\"claims_without_rubric_match\"] += not for reference, is_support in references:\n             counts[\"citation_count\"] += 1\n             counts[\"existing_citations\"] += reference in known\n             counts[\"available_citations\"] support_relationship_precision=ratio(counts[\"support_relationship_matches\"], counts[\"supporting_citation_count\"]),\n         contradiction_relationship_precision=ratio(counts[\"contradiction_relationship_matches\"], counts[\"contradicting_citation_count\"]),\n         rubric_fact_support=ratio(counts[\"witnessed_fact_count\"], counts[\"recognized_fact_count\"]),\n     )\n \n \n def score_run(\n     run: InvestigationRun | None, expected: ExpectedCase, rubric: CaseRubric,\n     catalog: IncidentCatalog, *, elapsed: float, error: str | None = None,\n ) -> RunMetrics:\n     answerable = expected.outcome == \"resolved\"\n     if run is None:\n         timed_out = bool(error and error.startswith(\"TimeoutError:\"))\n         return RunMetrics(\n             answerable=answerable, top_ranked_correct=False if answerable else None,\n             abstained=None, intentionally_inconclusive_handled=False if not answerable else None,\n             top_category=None, grounding=GroundingScore(), tool_calls=None, llm_calls=None,\n     or elapsed >= trace.budget.max_elapsed_seconds\n     )\n     cancelled = trace.termination_reason == \"cancelled\"\n     terminal = (\n         exhausted or cancelled or error is not None\n report.hypotheses[0] if report.hypotheses else None\n     matched = tuple(fact.fact_id for fact in rubric.facts if top and fact.matches(top.claim))\n     abstained = report.outcome == \"inconclusive\"\n     correct = (\n         not abstained and not terminal and top is not None\n         and top.cause_category == rubric.expected_category\n         and set(rubric.required_fact_ids) <= set(matched)\n     )\n     handled = (\n         abstained and not terminal and any(\n             re.search(pattern, \" \".join(report.limitations), re.IGNORECASE)\n             for pattern in rubric.abstention_patterns\n         )\n     )\n     calls = trace.model_calls\n     live = trace.execution_mode == \"live\"\n     unknown_calls = sum(not item.usage_measured for item in calls)\n     if len(calls) != trace.state.usage.llm_calls:\n         raise ValueError(\"model call count does not match the trace\")\n     if sum(task.attempts for task in trace.state.tasks if task.spec.query) != trace.state.usage.tool_calls:\n         raise ValueError(\"tool call count does not match task attempts\")\n     measured_input = sum(item.input_tokens for item in calls if item.usage_measured)\n     measured_output = sum(item.output_tokens for item in calls if item.usage_measured)\n     if (measured_input, measured_output) != (\n         trace.state.usage.input_tokens, trace.state.usage.output_tokens\n     ):\n         raise ValueError(\"provider usage counters do not match call traces\")\n     has_reported_usage = live and (not calls or any(item.usage_measured for grounding=grounding_score(run, rubric, evidence_index(catalog, expected.incident_id)),\n         tool_calls=trace.state.usage.tool_calls, llm_calls=trace.state.usage.llm_calls,\n         wall_clock_seconds=elapsed,\n         provider_input_tokens=measured_input if has_reported_usage else None,\n         provider_output_tokens=measured_output if has_reported_usage else None,\n         provider_usage_complete=live and unknown_calls == 0,\n         unmeasured_llm_calls=unknown_calls if live else None,\n         unmeasured_token_reservations=trace.state.usage.unmeasured_token_reservations,\n         charged_tokens=trace.state.usage.tokens,\n         had_failure=had_failure or terminal, terminal_failure=terminal,\n         failure_count=len(trace.failures) + (error is not None), budget_exhausted=exhausted,\n         status=(\n             \"budget_exhausted\" if exhausted else \"cancelled\" if cancelled else \"failed\" if terminal\n             else \"completed_with_failures\" if had_failure else \"completed\"\n         ),\n         termination_reason=trace.termination_reason,\n     )\n \n \n def distribution(values):\n     present = [value for value in values if value is not None]\n     return {\n         \"n\": len(present), \"missing\": len(values) - len(present),\n         \"mean\": mean(present) if present else None,\n         \"sample_stddev\": stdev(present) if len(present) > 1 else None,\n         \"min\": for row in selected if row.repetition == repetition]\n             answerable = [item for item in batch if item.answerable]\n             intentional = [item for item in batch if not ## 2026-11-07T09:29:42.146Z - assistant.message

Event ID: `7a678de6-272b-4adb-b677-bef228ae301c`

I found several concrete gaps: a revision can silently drop earlier evidence references, completed worker results can be lost during cancellation, and model-call reservations are not fully atomic. Dependent tool batches also fail instead of scheduling their prerequisites, and some CLI file errors produce tracebacks. I’ll add focused regressions and fix these without expanding the architecture.

No need to build your own orchestration—you define agent behavior, Copilot handles planning, tool invocation, file edits, and more.\n\n## Available SDKs\n\n[](#available-sdks)\n\n| SDK docs](https://javadoc.io/doc/com.github/copilot-sdk-java/latest/)                  |\n\nSee the individual SDK READMEs for installation, usage examples, and API reference.\n\n## Getting Started\n\n[](#getting-started)\n\nFor a complete walkthrough, see the **[Getting Started Guide](/github/copilot-sdk/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md)**.\n\nQuick steps:\n\n1.  **(Optional) Install the Copilot CLI**\n\nFor Node.js, Python, and .NET SDKs, the Copilot CLI is bundled automatically and no separate installation is required. The Rust SDK bundles the CLI by default through its `bundled-cli` feature. For Go, embed the CLI with the [bundler tool](/github/copilot-sdk/blob/main/go/README.md#distributing-your-application-with-an-embedded-github-copilot-cli); for Java, add the `com.github:copilot-sdk-java-runtime` dependency with your platform's classifier. Alternatively, [install the CLI manually](https://github.com/features/copilot/cli) and give the SDK its path with `COPILOT_CLI_PATH` or the client's CLI path option. The SDKs do not look up `copilot` on your PATH.\n\n2.  **Install your preferred SDK** using the commands above.\n\n3.  **See the SDK README** for usage examples and API documentation.\n\n## Architecture\n\n[](#architecture)\n\nAll SDKs drive the Copilot agent runtime over JSON-RPC. By default the runtime is hosted by the Copilot CLI running as a child process in server mode:\n\n```\nYour Application\n       ↓\n  SDK Client\n       ↓ JSON-RPC\n  Copilot CLI (server mode)\n```\n\nThe SDK manages the CLI process lifecycle automatically. You can also connect to an external CLI server—see the [Getting Started Guide](/github/copilot-sdk/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md#connecting-to-an-external-cli-server) for details on running the CLI in server mode.\n\nEvery SDK also offers an experimental in-process transport. It loads the native Copilot runtime into your application through a C ABI and carries the same JSON-RPC messages over an in-memory connection, so no CLI process is started:\n\n```\nYour Application\n       ↓\n  SDK Client\n       ↓ JSON-RPC (in memory, C ABI)\n  Native Copilot runtime\n```\n\nSee [Run the Copilot runtime in process](/github/copilot-sdk/blob/main/docs/setup/in-process-runtime.md) for the connection option in each language and its requirements.\n\n### Portable elicitation schemas\n\n[](#portable-elicitation-schemas)\n\nFor form elicitation callbacks, the portable schema contract is an object form with modeled `properties` and optional `required` fields (`type: \"object\"` on the wire; an SDK may represent the object type implicitly). Applications that support multiple SDK languages must use the modeled property definitions and must not depend on additional schema metadata (such as a top-level `title`) or on the insertion order of `properties`.\n\nNode.js and Rust pass through the wire schema, including additional metadata and property order. Python, Go, .NET, and Java reconstruct the callback schema from the modeled fields and do not offer that same preservation guarantee. Treat wire-schema preservation as a language-specific capability, not a cross-language requirement.\n\n### Agent Finder Skill installation APIs\n\n[](#agent-finder-skill-installation-apis)\n\nRuntimes that grant `skill-confirmed-installation` expose `skills.planInstall`, `skills.applyInstall`, `skills.planUninstall`, `skills.applyUninstall`, `skills.installations.list/recover/status/cancel`, and `skills.installations.setEnabled`. Skill install reviews include the full verified `SKILL.md` content up to 256 KiB, catalogue identity, file manifest, and non-absolute personal target location. Summaries report `ownershipState`, `configuredEnabled`, `sessionState`, retained catalogue identity and `installedAt`.\n\n## FAQ\n\n[](#faq)\n\n### Do I need a GitHub Copilot subscription to use the SDK?\n\n[](#do-i-need-a-github-copilot-subscription-to-use-the-sdk)\n\nYes, a GitHub Copilot subscription is required to use the GitHub Copilot SDK, **unless you are using BYOK (Bring Your Own Key)**. With BYOK, you can use the SDK without GitHub authentication by configuring your own API keys from supported LLM providers. For standard usage (non-BYOK), refer to the [GitHub Copilot pricing page](https://github.com/features/copilot#pricing), which includes a free tier with limited usage.\n\n### How does billing work for SDK usage?\n\n[](#how-does-billing-work-for-sdk-usage)\n\nBilling for the GitHub Copilot SDK is based on the same model as the Copilot CLI, with each prompt being counted towards your usage allowance. For more information on Copilot usage billing, see [Usage in GitHub Copilot](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/copilot-billing/models-and-pricing).\n\n### Does it support BYOK (Bring Your Own Key)?\n\n[](#does-it-support-byok-bring-your-own-key)\n\nYes, the GitHub Copilot SDK supports BYOK (Bring Your Own Key). You can configure the SDK to use your own API keys from supported LLM providers (e.g. OpenAI, Microsoft Foundry, Anthropic) to access models through those providers. See the **[BYOK documentation](/github/copilot-sdk/blob/main/docs/auth/byok.md)** for setup instructions and examples.\n\n**Note:** BYOK uses key-based authentication only. Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD), managed identities, and third-party identity providers are not supported.\n\n### What authentication methods are supported?\n\n[](#what-authentication-methods-are-supported)\n\nThe SDK supports multiple authentication methods:\n\n*   **GitHub signed-in user** - Uses stored OAuth credentials from `copilot` CLI login\n*   **OAuth GitHub App** - Pass user tokens from your GitHub OAuth app\n*   **Environment variables** - `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GH_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`\n*   **BYOK** - Use your own API keys (no GitHub auth required)\n\nSee the **[Authentication documentation](/github/copilot-sdk/blob/main/docs/auth/README.md)** for details on each method.\n\n### Do I need to install the Copilot CLI separately?\n\n[](#do-i-need-to-install-the-copilot-cli-separately)\n\nNo — for Node.js, Python, and .NET SDKs, the Copilot CLI is bundled automatically as a dependency. You do not need to install it separately.\n\nThe Rust SDK bundles the CLI by default through its `bundled-cli` feature.\n\nFor Go and Java SDKs, the CLI is **not** bundled by default. Go embeds it with its bundler tool, and Java uses the `com.github:copilot-sdk-java-runtime` dependency with your platform's classifier. Otherwise, install the CLI manually and give the SDK its path with `COPILOT_CLI_PATH` or the client's CLI path option. The SDKs do not look up `copilot` on your PATH.\n\nAdvanced: You can override the CLI binary or connect to an external server. See the individual SDK README for language-specific options.\n\n### What tools are enabled by default?\n\n[](#what-tools-are-enabled-by-default)\n\nBy default, the SDK exposes the Copilot CLI's first-party tools, similar to running the CLI with `--allow-all`. Tool execution is still governed by each SDK's permission handler, so applications can approve, deny, or customize tool calls. You can customize tool availability by configuring the SDK client options to enable and disable specific tools. Refer to the individual SDK documentation for details on tool configuration and to the Copilot CLI documentation for the list of available tools.\n\n### Can I use custom agents, skills or tools?\n\n[](#can-i-use-custom-agents-skills-or-tools)\n\nYes, the GitHub Copilot SDK allows you to define custom agents, skills, and tools. You can extend the functionality of the agents by implementing your own logic and integrating additional tools as needed. Refer to the SDK documentation of your preferred language for more details.\n\n### Are there instructions or SDK guidance for Copilot to speed up development?\n\n[](#are-there-instructions-or-sdk-guidance-for-copilot-to-speed-up-development)\n\nYes, check out the custom instructions and SDK-specific guidance:\n\n*   **[Node.js / TypeScript](https://github.com/github/awesome-copilot/blob/main/instructions/copilot-sdk-nodejs.instructions.md)**\n*   **[Python](https://github.com/github/awesome-copilot/blob/main/instructions/copilot-sdk-python.instructions.md)**\n*   **[.NET](https://github.com/github/awesome-copilot/blob/main/instructions/copilot-sdk-csharp.instructions.md)**\n*   **[Go](https://github.com/github/awesome-copilot/blob/main/instructions/copilot-sdk-go.instructions.md)**\n*   **[Rust](/github/copilot-sdk/blob/main/rust/README.md)** (SDK guidance; custom instructions not yet published)\n*   **[Java](https://github.com/github/awesome-copilot/blob/main/instructions/copilot-sdk-java.instructions.md)**\n\n### What models are supported?\n\n[](#what-models-are-supported)\n\nAll models available via Copilot CLI are supported in the SDK. The SDK also exposes a method which will return the models available so they can be accessed at runtime.\n\n### Is the SDK production-ready?\n\n[](#is-the-sdk-production-ready)\n\nThe GitHub Copilot SDK is generally available and follows semantic versioning. After installing, download the\nruntime:\n\n```bash\npython -m copilot download-runtime\n```\n\nThis downloads the platform release package, verifies it against the release's\n`SHA256SUMS.txt`, and directly stages `copilot-runtime`, its adjacent `runtime.node`,\nand the filtered hostless runtime assets locally without retaining the downloaded\narchive. If you skip this step, the SDK performs the same staging automatically on\nfirst managed stdio/TCP use.\n\nTo pre-provision the native library required by the in-process (FFI) transport\n(see [In-process (FFI) transport](#in-process-ffi-transport)), pass `--in-process`:\n\n```bash\npython -m copilot download-runtime --in-process\n```\n\nThis also creates a `copilot` compatibility entrypoint from `copilot-runtime`\ninside the complete materialized bundle. Its adjacent `runtime.node` can then be\nused for in-process hosting. That canonical staged library is reused, so this does\nnot download a second runtime artifact.\n\n| Platform | Cache path |\n|----------|-----------|\n| Linux | `~/.cache/github-copilot-sdk/cli/<version>/prebuilds/<platform>/` |\n| macOS | `~/Library/Caches/github-copilot-sdk/cli/<version>/prebuilds/<platform>/` |\n| Windows | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\\github-copilot-sdk\\cli\\<version>\\prebuilds\\<platform>\\` |\n\n### Environment variables\n\n| Variable | Description |\n|----------|-------------|\n| `COPILOT_CLI_PATH` | Use this specific binary instead of downloading |\n| `COPILOT_CLI_EXTRACT_DIR` | Override the version-specific cache directory |\n| `COPILOT_SKIP_CLI_DOWNLOAD` | Set to `1` to disable auto-download |\n| `COPILOT_CLI_DOWNLOAD_BASE_URL` | Override the GitHub Releases download URL used for the runtime package and checksums |\n\n## Run the Sample\n\nTry the interactive chat sample (from the repo root):\n\n```bash\ncd python/samples\npython chat.py\n```\n\n## Quick Start\n\nFor experimental in-process AHP hosting, use `client.start_ahp_host(AhpHostOptions(...))`.\nSet `authentication=AhpHostAuthentication(mode)` with `\"github\"`, `\"none\"`, or\n`\"custom\"` in every client mode. Custom policies require a stable nonempty `require_identity`\nand async `authenticate(request)`: return `AhpAuthenticationResult(identity, expires_at)`\nwith that exact identity and a future RFC3339 expiration, or `None` to reject.\nThe request contains the decrypted admission `token` and an `asyncio.Event`\n(`cancellation_event`) set when validation ends. Exceptions reject access.\nImport these handwritten types from `copilot`. Admission tokens never configure\nGitHub authentication or inference. Factories receive trusted `request.authentication`\nbeside `request.config`, never inside it. Select `local_server=HostLocalServerOptions()`,\n`github_environment=HostGitHubEnvironmentOptions(name=\"My app\", compute_id=\"stable-installation-id\")`\nfor Mission Control/WPS (GitHub authentication only), or both; import transports\nfrom `copilot.rpc`. At least one transport is required. GitHub-only hosts have no\n`url` or `token`; `host.environment_id` identifies their environment.\n`await host.list_sessions()` lists live and dormant sessions. Top-level `compute_id`\nreuses the durable catalog across transports and must match `github_environment.compute_id`.\nOmitted local identities persist. Dormant application publications need a resume callback.\nSee [runtime-supervised AHP hosting](../docs/runtime-supervised-host.md) for creation\nand resume callbacks, resident-session publication, ownership, and shared-snapshot E2Es.\n\n```python\nimport asyncio\n\nfrom copilot import CopilotClient\nfrom copilot.session_events import (\n    AssistantMessageData,\n    SessionAutopilotStoppedData,\n    SessionIdleData,\n    SessionMode,\n)\nfrom copilot.session import PermissionHandler\n\n\nasync def main():\n    # Client automatically starts on enter and cleans up on exit\n    async with CopilotClient() as client:\n        # Create a session with automatic cleanup\n        async with await client.create_session(\n            on_permission_request=PermissionHandler.approve_all,\n            model=\"gpt-5\",\n        ) as session:\n            # Wait for non-Autopilot idle or this request's Autopilot stop\n            request_id = None\n            pending = []\n            done = asyncio.Event()\n\n            def observe(event):\n                match event.data:\n                    case AssistantMessageData() as data:\n                        print(data.content)\n                    case SessionIdleData() as data if data.mode != SessionMode.AUTOPILOT:\n                        done.set()\n                    case SessionAutopilotStoppedData() as data if (\n                        request_id and data.request_id == request_id\n                    ):\n                        done.set()\n\n            def on_event(event):\n                if event.agent_id:\n                    return\n                if request_id is None and isinstance(\n                    event.data, (SessionIdleData, SessionAutopilotStoppedData)\n                ):\n                    pending.append(event)\n                else:\n                    observe(event)\n\n            session.on(on_event)\n            request_id = await session.send(\"What is 2+2?\")\n            for event in pending:\n                observe(event)\n            pending.clear()\n            await done.wait()\n\n\nasyncio.run(main())\n```\n\n### Message source\n\nUse `AgentMessageSource(agent_id)` for messages from an identified agent.\nUse `source=\"system\"` for application-internal context, not as a substitute for\nagent provenance. Both `send` and `send_and_wait` accept the optional\n`MessageSource` type:\n\n```python\nfrom copilot import AgentMessageSource, MessageSource\n\nsource: MessageSource = AgentMessageSource(\"reviewer\")\nawait session.send(\"Review complete\", source=source)\nawait session.send_and_wait(\"Review findings attached\", source=source)\nawait session.send(\"Workspace context updated\", source=\"system\")\n```\n\n`AgentMessageSource` is immutable and requires a string ID. The SDK sends the ID\nunchanged after the `agent-` prefix, so `\"reviewer\"` becomes `\"agent-reviewer\"`.\nIt does not trim whitespace, change case, or remove an existing prefix.\n\nLeave source unset (or `None`) for ordinary human sends so the field stays omitted.\nUse `\"user\"` when you need to set it explicitly. Source is independent of delivery\nmode and does not replace the session's `system_message` configuration, set billing\nflags, or use the notification API. `send_and_wait` can return `None` when the\nrequest completes without an assistant message, at non-Autopilot idle or its\nmatching Autopilot stop; errors still propagate.\nSub-agent events remain visible to listeners but do not complete the wait\nor supply its reply.\n\n### Manual Resource Management\n\nIf you need more control over the lifecycle, you can call `start()`, `stop()`, and `disconnect()` manually:\n\nFor an SDK-owned stdio runtime, `stop()` and async context-manager exit request\nshutdown, close stdin, and wait up to 10 seconds for the process to finish host\ncleanup, including telemetry flushing. A process that does not exit is terminated,\nthen killed if necessary, with bounded waits. `force_stop()` skips graceful cleanup;\nexternally managed runtimes are not shut down.\nIt disconnects retained sessions locally, releases their registered callbacks, and\nfails pending `send_and_wait()` calls without waiting for idle or their response timeout.\nDisconnected sessions reject new event subscriptions.\n\n```python\nimport asyncio\n\nfrom copilot import CopilotClient\nfrom copilot.session_events import (\n    AssistantMessageData,\n    SessionAutopilotStoppedData,\n    SessionIdleData,\n    SessionMode,\n)\nfrom copilot.session import PermissionHandler\n\n\nasync def main():\n    client = CopilotClient()\n    await client.start()\n\n    # approve_all is only valid when managed settings are disabled.\n    session = await client.create_session(\n        on_permission_request=PermissionHandler.approve_all,\n        model=\"gpt-5\",\n    )\n\n    request_id = None\n    pending = []\n    done = asyncio.Event()\n\n    def observe(event):\n        match event.data:\n            case AssistantMessageData() as data:\n                print(data.content)\n            case SessionIdleData() as data if data.mode != SessionMode.AUTOPILOT:\n                done.set()\n            case SessionAutopilotStoppedData() as data if (\n                request_id and data.request_id == request_id\n            ):\n                done.set()\n\n    def on_event(event):\n        if event.agent_id:\n            return\n        if request_id is None and isinstance(\n            event.data, (SessionIdleData, SessionAutopilotStoppedData)\n        ):\n            pending.append(event)\n        else:\n            observe(event)\n\n    session.on(on_event)\n    request_id = await session.send(\"What is 2+2?\")\n    for event in pending:\n        observe(event)\n    pending.clear()\n    await done.wait()\n\n    # Clean up manually\n    await session.disconnect()\n    await client.stop()\n\n\nasyncio.run(main())\n```\n\n## Features\n\n- ✅ Full JSON-RPC protocol support\n- ✅ stdio, TCP, and in-process (FFI) transports\n- ✅ Real-time streaming events\n- ✅ Session history with `get_events()`\n- ✅ Type hints throughout\n- ✅ Async/await native\n- ✅ Async context manager support for automatic resource cleanup\n\n### Skill providers (experimental)\n\nSkill providers let a session serve skills from SDK-owned storage instead of\n`SKILL.md` files on disk. Implement `SkillProvider`, return generated\n`SkillProviderDescriptor` values from `list_skills()`, and return the skill\nmarkdown from `read_skill(name)`. Both methods can be sync or async; keep sync\nproviders fast because they run on the event loop.\n\n```python\nimport asyncio\n\nfrom copilot import CopilotClient, SkillProvider, SkillProviderDescriptor\n\n\nclass MemorySkills(SkillProvider):\n    def list_skills(self):\n        return [\n            SkillProviderDescriptor(\n                name=\"release-notes\",\n                description=\"Draft release notes from recent changes\",\n            )\n        ]\n\n    async def read_skill(self, name: str) -> str | None:\n        if name != \"release-notes\":\n            return None\n        return \"Draft concise release notes with highlights and migration notes.\"\n\n\nasync def main():\n    async with CopilotClient(mode=\"empty\", base_directory=\"./.copilot-empty\") as client:\n        async with await client.create_session(\n            available_tools=[],\n            enable_skills=True,\n            skill_provider=MemorySkills(),\n        ) as session:\n            await session.send(\"Use /release-notes for this change set\")\n\n\nasyncio.run(main())\n```\n\nIn `\"empty\"` mode, set `enable_skills=True`; otherwise the provider is bound but\ndormant. Providers are ephemeral and are not persisted, so pass `skill_provider=`\nagain to `resume_session()`. Cloud sessions do not support skill providers.\nProviders must be safe for concurrent calls because the runtime may list or read\nskills from multiple agent paths at the same time. When the runtime cancels a\ncall, for example after its 30-second limit or when the session disconnects, an\nasync provider's task is cancelled and receives `asyncio.CancelledError`. Closing\nthe connection or force-stopping the client doesn't cancel a running call; it\ncontinues until it returns.\n\n#### Supporting files (experimental)\n\nTo give a provider skill supporting files, such as scripts, references,\ntemplates, and assets, set its descriptor's `directory` to the absolute path of\nthe folder that holds them:\n\n```python\nfrom copilot import SkillProviderDescriptor\n\nSkillProviderDescriptor(\n    name=\"release-notes\",\n    description=\"Writes release notes in the team's format.\",\n    directory=\"/srv/skills/release-notes\",\n)\n```\n\nWhen the skill is activated, the runtime lists the folder's files for the model.\nSee [Supporting files](../docs/features/skills.md#supporting-files-experimental) for details.\n\n## API Reference\n\n### CopilotClient\n\n```python\nfrom copilot import CopilotClient\nfrom copilot.session import PermissionHandler\n\nasync with CopilotClient() as client:\n    async with await client.create_session(\n        on_permission_request=PermissionHandler.approve_all,\n        model=\"gpt-5\",\n    ) as session:\n\n        def on_event(event):\n            print(f\"Event: {event.type}\")\n\n        session.on(on_event)\n        await session.send(\"Hello!\")\n\n        # ... wait for events ...\n```\n\n> **Note:** For manual lifecycle management, see [Manual Resource Management](#manual-resource-management) above.\n\n```python\nfrom copilot import CopilotClient, RuntimeConnection\n\n# Connect to an existing CLI server\nclient = CopilotClient(connection=RuntimeConnection.for_uri(\"localhost:3000\"))\n```\n\n**CopilotClient Constructor:**\n\n<!-- docs-validate: hidden -->\n```python\nfrom copilot import CopilotClient, RuntimeConnection\n\nCopilotClient()  # spawn the bundled runtime with defaults\nCopilotClient(connection=RuntimeConnection.for_stdio(), log_level=\"debug\", github_token=\"token\")\n```\n<!-- /docs-validate: hidden -->\n\n```python\nCopilotClient()                                                   # spawn the bundled runtime with defaults\nCopilotClient(connection=..., log_level=\"debug\", github_token=..., ...)\n```\n\nAll options are kw-only parameters:\n\n- `connection` (RuntimeConnection | None): How to reach the runtime. Use\n  `RuntimeConnection.for_stdio(...)`, `RuntimeConnection.for_tcp(...)`,\n  `RuntimeConnection.for_uri(...)`, or `RuntimeConnection.for_inprocess(...)`.\n  Defaults to a stdio connection with the bundled binary.\n- `working_directory` (str | None): Working directory for the CLI process (default: current dir).\n- `log_level` (str): Log level (default: \"info\").\n- `env` (dict | None): Environment variables for the CLI process.\n\n    For the native standalone runtime, include\n    `{\"COPILOT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED\": \"true\"}` in `env` before startup to\n    disable Copilot-owned GitHub and Entra authentication telemetry process-wide, including\n    sessionless events. Authentication, `on_github_telemetry` forwarding, and\n    user-configured OpenTelemetry export remain unchanged. This is separate from\n    `enable_session_telemetry=False`, which disables only a session's pipeline.\n    The value must be exactly `\"true\"`; changing it requires a process restart.\n    `COPILOT_GITHUB_TELEMETRY_DISABLED` remains native-runtime/GitHub-only. In-process connections reject\n    per-client `env`; set the variable in the host process environment before\n    starting the runtime instead.\n\n- `github_token` (str | None): GitHub token for authentication. When provided, takes priority over other auth methods.\n- `base_directory` (str | None): Base directory for Copilot data (session state, config, etc.). Sets `COPILOT_HOME` on the spawned CLI process. When `None`, the CLI defaults to `~/.copilot`. Useful in restricted environments where only specific directories are writable. Ignored when using a `UriRuntimeConnection`.\n- `extension_launch_provider` (ExtensionLaunchProviderHandler | None): Experimental connection-level resolver for extension launch profiles. The client installs the reverse-RPC handler and registers the provider during startup before sessions can be created.\n- `installation_confirmation_handler` (InstallationConfirmationHandler | None): Experimental connection-global human review for `installations.confirm`. Receives the typed request and one cancellation signal, and returns an explicit decision. Does not enable installation capabilities.\n- `network` (NetworkConfig | None): Experimental. Network callbacks through which the SDK host decides the runtime's proxies and supplies its Kerberos tokens. The client installs the `network.resolveProxy` and `network.authenticateNegotiate` handlers and registers the configured callbacks and `scope` during startup before sessions can be created. See [Network callbacks](#network-callbacks-experimental).\n- `use_logged_in_user` (bool | None): Whether to use logged-in user for authentication (default: True, but False when `github_token` is provided).\n- `telemetry` (dict | None): OpenTelemetry configuration for the CLI process. Providing this enables telemetry — no separate flag needed. See [Telemetry](#telemetry) below.\n- `session_fs` (dict | None): Connection-level session filesystem provider configuration. To let `view` read provider-only images, set `capabilities.binary` to `True` and return a provider implementing `SessionFsBinaryProvider` (`read_file_bytes(path)` and `write_file_bytes(path, content, mode=None)`) from `create_session_fs_handler`; image reads do not fall back to local files. Binary reads and writes are limited to 50,330,880 raw bytes (approximately 48 MiB); larger results return a filesystem error before encoding or decoding.\n- `session_idle_timeout_seconds` (int | None): Server-wide session idle timeout in seconds. Set to `None` or `0` to disable.\n- `on_list_models` (callable | None): Custom handler for `list_models()`. When provided, the handler is called instead of querying the runtime.\n- `mode` (str): Client mode (default: `\"copilot-cli\"`).\n\n**RuntimeConnection variants:**\n\n- `RuntimeConnection.for_stdio(path=None, args=None)` — spawn a local CLI process and talk over stdio.\n- `RuntimeConnection.for_tcp(port=0, connection_token=None, path=None, args=None)` — spawn a local CLI in TCP mode.\n- `RuntimeConnection.for_uri(url, connection_token=None)` — connect to an existing CLI server (e.g. `\"localhost:8080\"`).\n- `RuntimeConnection.for_inprocess()` — host the runtime in-process via its native C ABI (FFI). See [In-process (FFI) transport](#in-process-ffi-transport).\n\nManaged stdio and TCP connections use the downloaded `copilot-runtime`\nexecutable with adjacent `runtime.node` by default. An explicit connection\npath or `COPILOT_CLI_PATH` overrides the downloaded runtime.\n\nChild-process connections (`for_stdio`/`for_tcp`) also expose a per-connection\n`env` field for the spawned process. Set it on the returned connection instead of\nthe client-level `env` — setting both raises. The mapping replaces the child's\nentire environment rather than adding to it, so start from `os.environ` to keep\nthe variables the runtime needs, such as `PATH`:\n\n```python\nimport os\n\nfrom copilot import CopilotClient, RuntimeConnection\n\nconn = RuntimeConnection.for_stdio()\nconn.env = {**os.environ, \"MY_VAR\": \"value\"}\nclient = CopilotClient(connection=conn)  # do NOT also pass env=... here\n```\n\n### Installation confirmation (experimental)\n\nSet `installation_confirmation_handler` on `CopilotClient` to receive the\nruntime's `installations.confirm` callback through\n`InstallationConfirmationHandler`. The handler receives the generated\n`InstallationConfirmationRequest` and an `InstallationConfirmationContext`, and\nreturns only an explicit `InstallationDecision` (or `\"confirm\"`, `\"decline\"` or\n`\"cancel\"`). The SDK echoes the original challenge and review fingerprint; it\nnever infers approval.\n\nMatch `operation_id` and `policy_session_id` against the original action on this\nexact connection before presenting the complete review. Missing legacy session\nmetadata does not select a default session. Refuse unknown operations or\nincomplete reviews. Concurrent reviews are independent and do not block the\nrequest router.\n\n`context.cancelled` is an `asyncio.Event` set when this review is retired,\nwhether by the runtime's numeric `$/cancelRequest`, runtime-enforced expiry, or\nloss of the original connection. Separately spawned UI work must observe this\nsignal and close itself when it is set. A late handler result cannot approve a\nretired request. Dropping an outbound installation or OAuth future does not\ncancel that operation.\n\nCall `client.rpc.mcp.prepare_install(...)` before `apply_install(...)`.\n\n<note>Content truncated. Here is the raw content:\nContents of https://raw.githubusercontent.com/github/copilot-sdk/d1e6021a43b26e87acfcd43b37988eff09dd8aaf/docs/setup/multi-tenancy.md:\n# Multi-tenancy and server deployments\n\nMulti-user server mode means running the Copilot SDK from backend code that serves more than one human, tenant, workspace, or integration account. In this setup, the application owns request routing and authorization, while the SDK and runtime provide per-session state, per-session authentication, and explicit tool registration so one user's session does not inherit another user's tools or identity.\n\n**Best for:** SaaS products, partner integrations, internal platforms, and backend services that handle concurrent users.\n\n## Use this guide when\n\nUse this guide when you are building:\n\n* A multi-user SaaS product that embeds Copilot-powered agents\n* A backend for a partner integration, such as a Copilot Studio or Fabric-style pattern\n* Any server that handles concurrent users, workspaces, tenants, or requests\n* A shared runtime where multiple SDK clients connect to one Copilot runtime process\n\nThis guide is a sister to [Scaling and multi-tenancy](./scaling.md). Use this guide for SDK-level options and runtime isolation choices.\n\n## Key SDK options\n\n| Option | Use it for | Notes |\n|--------|------------|-------|\n| `mode: \"empty\"` | Disabling ambient OS tools and CLI defaults | Required for multi-user or shared scenarios. |\n| `sessionIdleTimeoutSeconds` | Cleaning idle sessions | Set a server-side timeout for long-running processes. |\n| `baseDirectory` | Isolating `COPILOT_HOME` per runtime instance | Ignored when connecting to an existing runtime. |\n| `sessionFs` | Routing session filesystem storage off local disk | Pair with per-session filesystem providers. |\n| `RuntimeConnection.forUri(url)` | Sharing one already-running runtime | Language names vary; see samples below. |\n| `memory.storeMemory` | Keeping agent memories in application storage | Your app owns storage, isolation and recall. |\n| Per-session GitHub token or provider | Scoping auth to the requesting user | Prefer a rotating provider for short-lived credentials; use a static `gitHubToken` only when rotation is unnecessary. |\n\nFor callback-backed credentials, see [Rotating session-scoped GitHub tokens](../auth/authenticate.md#rotating-session-scoped-github-tokens).
