Ranked hypotheses require\n supporting observations. Citation existence is checked, **not semantic entailment**:\n the Critic provides model-based scrutiny, not a proof. Unresolved critical objections,\n missing critical analysis, terminal source failures or inability to produce a valid\n report force an inconclusive outcome with explicit limitations. A missing model\n report yields a clearly marked runtime fallback, not a diagnosis.\n \n ### Shared investigation standards\n \n Both approaches explicitly label hypotheses as `initiating_cause`, `mechanism`\n or `unknown`, and record `blocking_uncertainties` separately from assumptions.\n `residual_uncertainties` captures ordinary remaining uncertainty without asserting\n that a supported conclusion is impossible. A blocking gap must identify a specific\n missing fact that could change cause selection or distinguish an evidence-backed\n alternative. Hypothetical unobserved concurrent factors, without a concrete lead,\n do not automatically block a conclusion. Unperformed confirmation experiments\n are not automatically blocking either. Classification still requires judgment:\n real gaps must not be relabeled merely to allow higher confidence.\n The cause claim should explain the trigger/causal condition and its link to the\n observed mechanism, rather than merely name an error. Mechanism-only, unknown or\n blocked candidates must have confidence at most **0.6**, and cannot be the winner\n of an ordinary ranked root-cause report. This fixed provisional ceiling is a\n conservative consistency policy, **not confidence calibration or semantic proof**.\n An initiating-cause label is still a model judgment; Python cannot verify causality.\n Prompts ask for evidence-backed competing hypotheses when warranted, not a minimum\n candidate count or impossible proof that arbitrary unobserved causes do not exist.\n \n Affected services are starting points, not an allowlist. Prompts expose service\n scopes and dependency edges derived solely from the context and acquired ledger.\n Both investigators can request downstream evidence using those leads; no hidden\n dataset inventory, ground truth or case-specific selection rule is supplied.\n Existing role permissions, dependency checks, deduplication, attempts and total\n budgets still govern these queries.\n \n Reporting receives canonical runtime limitations, including coverage gaps,\n failed tasks and unresolved critical objections. Both prompts discourage\n paraphrased repetition; runtime deduplication normalizes whitespace, case and\n terminal punctuation. Distinct gaps are retained. There is no fuzzy semantic\n deduplicator that could silently erase different uncertainties.\n \n The baseline repeatedly chooses queries, inspects results, revises hypotheses and\n finishes using the same report schema. Its tool calls execute sequentially. It gets\n the same incident context, suggested windows, tool records and total resource\n ceilings, without separate specialist/Critic roles. Each CLI run creates fresh tools,\n resetting injected failures. Evaluation must use the same model, settings and budget\n and a fresh tool instance for each approach.\n \n ## Runtime ceilings and recovery\n \n | Ceiling | Default (both approaches) |\n | --- | --- |\n | Total tool calls | 30 |\n | Total LLM calls, including transient failures and correction | 24 |\n | Total charged/reserved tokens | 120,000 |\n | Maximum output tokens per model call | 1,500 |\n | Overall investigation deadline | 120 seconds |\n | Per tool / per model timeout | 2 / 30 seconds |\n | Concurrent tools | 5 (baseline deliberately sequential) |\n | Attempts per operation/query, including correction | 3 total, not 3 retries |\n | Agent-output correction requests per logical operation | At most 1, within all existing ceilings |\n | Critic-driven follow-up rounds | 2 maximum |\n \n `ExecutionBudget` is injectable through either Python runner; the CLI uses these\n defaults. The baseline's iterative steps are bounded by the same LLM-call ceiling.\n The original low-level `TaskSpec` accepts up to five attempts for compatibility\n with foundation tests; agent/baseline runs always override it with the runtime\n three-attempt ceiling, shared across identical queries.\n \n SDK retries are disabled. Connection/timeout, HTTP 408/429 and server failures are\n retryable while resources remain. Authentication, refusal, incomplete output,\n invalid schemas/references/access and exhausted budgets are not transiently\n retryable. The narrow response-correction policy below is distinct from a\n transport retry and grants no additional budget. Model\n retry waits are bounded; local fixture tools need no backoff. Failed prerequisites\n block dependents. Independent sources can continue, and analyses can inspect error\n observations through successful-task dependencies rather than pretend a failed\n tool succeeded. Terminal failures are reported conservatively as inconclusive.\n Tool batches execute prerequisite-ready waves, regardless of input order, including\n in sequential mode. Blocked tasks have a structured dependency error and zero\n attempts. Adapter integration errors are visible, nonretryable operation failures,\n not empty successes. Model-call, attempt and token reservations share one atomic\n budget check. Responses are checked against the deadline before admission, and\n finalization cannot return ordinary success after the overall deadline.\n \n ### One bounded response correction\n \n The same coordinator policy applies to both approaches. Only two safe output-error\n classes are eligible: initial-plan specialist ownership mismatches, and hypothesis\n confidence/uncertainty consistency violations. Initial ownership recovery requires\n otherwise valid tasks, queries, incident scope, dependencies and uniqueness.\n Unknown evidence, cross-incident/unsafe access, wrong agent identity, arbitrary\n schema errors, authentication, refusal, incomplete output and budget exhaustion\n do not gain a correction path.\n \n The same logical task and agent receive their rejected response, concise validation\n errors, the required JSON contract and the original frozen evidence/context.\n The request asks for a corrected structured response, not new observations or a\n new diagnosis. There is at most **one actual correction request**; it is not\n reissued even if that request has a transient failure. Earlier transport retries\n and the correction share the same three-attempt limit, 24-call ceiling, token\n preflight and deadlines. Exhausted resources can prevent correction dispatch.\n The larger prompt, including rejected text and schema, is budgeted normally.\n \n Correction is explicit model work, not runtime editing. A corrected plan must\n retain task IDs and queries and return valid specialist assignments. A confidence\n correction must retain candidate IDs, causal claims/categories/stages, both\n evidence polarities and every uncertainty verbatim in blocking or residual fields.\n Any deliberate confidence revision or uncertainty reclassification requires a\n new written explanation. A corrected ranked report cannot retain a blocking\n initiating-cause gap. The runtime never deletes uncertainty or lowers confidence\n to manufacture validity, and does not verify the explanation's semantic quality.\n \n Every correction is revalidated before committing state. Both responses, original\n validation errors, measured usage and attempt numbers remain in the trace;\n `correction_of_attempt` identifies the correction's rejected attempt. Failed\n correction cannot overwrite previously accepted hypotheses or dispatch invalid\n tools and terminates transparently as inconclusive. Recovered errors remain\n visible; the unchanged evaluator labels nonterminal recovery\n `completed_with_failures` rather than silently excluding failures.\n \n Before dispatch, the coordinator reserves a conservative UTF-8 byte-based bound\n"

}

It chooses tools, inspects results, revises hypotheses\n and finishes, without specialist roles. Independent tool instances reset injected\n failures for fair comparisons.\n \n Ten local cases separate operational observations from evaluator-only answers.\n Historical resemblance and change timing are leads, not guaranteed causes.\n Mocked tests validate orchestration, not predictive accuracy. Citation validation\n cannot prove semantic grounding. The deterministic evaluator\n uses private expected facts and witness sets to distinguish citation existence\n from limited claim support, without a semantic judge. Categories are generic;\n the per-incident answer mapping never enters prompts. Query-keyed failure counters\n make injected errors independent of parallel scheduling. Paired repeated runs\n share model settings and total ceilings, retain failures, and save JSON/CSV,\n traces, manifests and variability. One live pilot pair completed without execution\n failures. Multi-agent identified a configuration trigger but abstained; baseline\n stopped at pool exhaustion. Baseline was cheaper and faster; one case establishes\n no general superiority. A second\n pair failed ownership and confidence validation; raw baseline reasoning named\n the trigger but was rejected. Neither pair earned root-cause credit. The remaining\n live cases, current recovery behavior and full benchmark are unverified.\n \n Causal stages, blocking versus residual uncertainty, critical-query links and\n explicit deferrals make uncertainty visible. A provisional confidence ceiling\n is a consistency policy, not calibration. Explanation quality and causal\n classification still depend on the model. Potential improvements are a larger\n independent corpus, empirical confidence calibration and targeted prompt revision\n from separately approved live measurements, not additional orchestration infrastructure.\n \n"

hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest() for path in sorted(set(paths))}\n+\n+\n+def systemic_error(status, code, error_type):\n+    billing_codes = {\n+        \"insufficient_quota\", \"billing_hard_limit_reached\", \"billing_not_active\",\n+        \"billing_error\", \"credit_balance_insufficient\", \"insufficient_credits\",\n+        \"usage_limit_reached\",\n+    }\n+    return status in {401, 402, 403} or bool({code, error_type} & billing_codes)\n+\n+\n+async def run(config, catalog, settings, truth, rubric):\n+    adapter = OpenAILLM(config.model, temperature=config.temperature)\n+    original_create = adapter.client.responses.create\n+    original_respond = adapter.respond\n+    sequence = 0\n+    active_run = None\n+    halted = None\n+    task_attempts = Counter()\n+    blocked = []\n+\n+    async def capture(**kwargs):\n+        nonlocal sequence, halted\n+        if halted:\n+            raise LLMFailure(\"benchmark_systemic_stop\", \"Provider access halted; no new HTTP request issued\")\n+        sequence += 1\n+        call_number = sequence\n+        task_id = json.loads(kwargs[\"input\"])[\"task_id\"]\n+        task_attempts[(active_run, task_id)] += 1\n+        record = {\n+            \"sequence\": call_number, \"run_id\": active_run, \"task_id\": task_id,\n+            \"provider_attempt_for_task\": task_attempts[(active_run, task_id)],\n+            \"requested_model\": kwargs[\"model\"], \"temperature\": kwargs[\"temperature\"],\n+            \"max_output_tokens\": original_create(**kwargs)\n+            record[\"response\"] = response.model_dump(mode=\"json\")\n+            return response\n+        except APIStatusError as exc:\n+            body = exc.body if error.get(\"code\") or \"\")\n+            error_type = str(error.get(\"type\") or \"\")\n+            record[\"failure\"] = {\n+                \"type\": type(exc).__name__, \"http_status\":         halted = {\n+                    \"run_id\": active_run, \"task_id\": task_id,\n+                    \"sequence\": call_number, \"failure\": record[\"failure\"],\n+                    \"detected_at\": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),\n+                }\n+                print(\"SYSTEMIC PROVIDER FAILURE: new paid requests halted\", flush=True)\n+            raise\n+ authentication/billing failure; remaining cases not started\")\n+        active_run = f\"{context.incident_id}.{approach}.{repetition:03d}\"\n+        print(f\"START {active_run}\", flush=True)\n+        return adapter\n+\n+    adapter.client.responses.create = capture\n+    adapter.respond = guarded_respond\n+    aborted = False\n+    try:\n+        rows = await evaluate(\n+            config, The direction of the observed comparison therefore\n+does not depend on including the repeatedly used development case. However, the\n+other nine are still part of the same known synthetic dataset, not an independent\n+external holdout.\n+\n+The baseline had lower measured mean latency and cost in both cohorts. Multi-agent\n+had higher limited citation-support precision and handled the intentional\n+inconclusive case appropriately, but these do not offset its observed execution\n+failures and answerable-case abstentions. This benchmark does not support claiming\n+multi-agent superiority.\n+\n+## Exact execution failures\n+\n+| Approach | Cases | Rejected operation and saved error |\n+| --- | --- | --- |\n+| Multi-agent | `inc-001` | Reasoning returned non-descending confidences (0.95 then 0.98). Its one correction failed `correction must explain its contract repair or uncertainty judgment`. Reporting produced a valid failure summary, not validated Reasoning analysis. |\n+| Multi-agent | `inc-003`, `inc-004`, `inc-010` | Critic returned `follow_up_indices: [0]` with an empty `follow_ups` list. The final single correction deleted/replaced a rejected candidate and failed `correction cannot replace or delete a rejected candidate`. |\n+\n+These are response/contract failures, not evidence that the provider failed.\n+Changing investigator code or recovery policy during the benchmark would have\n+invalidated the comparison; no such change was made.\n+\n+## Recovery and resource limits\n+\n+- Multi-agent used three correction requests; all three corrections were rejected.\n+- Baseline used nine correction requests: five accepted and four rejected. The five\n+  accepted corrections enabled progress but their investigations later failed.\n+- Each logical operation received at most one correction request. All corrections,\n+  including rejected ones, are included in measured tokens, latency and cost.\n+- Both approaches retried the transient `inc-007` metrics failure once and obtained\n+  evidence successfully. No tool, request, token or wall-clock\n+  budget was exhausted.\n+- Multi-agent's three completed runs stopped at the existing two-follow-up-round\n+  ceiling. `follow_up_round_limit` is a recorded resource-limit termination, not an\n+  execution-budget failure in those runs. Remaining critical gaps kept them\n+  inconclusive.\n+\n+## Citation validity is not claim support\n+\n+All emitted citations existed and had been acquired: **60/60** multi-agent and\n+**24/24** baseline. For example, baseline `inc-005`\n+passed the `resolver_domain_change` fact pattern by describing DNS failures for\n+`pricing.legacy.internal`, despite querying only logs/metrics and leaving the\n+origin of those failures as residual uncertainty. These are rubric\n+credits, not proof of a fully grounded initiating-cause explanation.\n+\n+## Confidence, uncertainty and recommendation safety\n+\n+- Baseline `inc-001`, `inc-004` and `inc-007` ranked an observed failure mechanism\n+  at confidence 0.9 while its initiating cause was absent or left as residual\n+  uncertainty. The runtime checks declared causal-stage labels; it does not\n+  semantically verify that the prose really describes an initiating cause.\n+- Multi-agent repeatedly treated hypothetical concurrent dependency issues as\n+  blocking without a concrete discriminating lead. `inc-002` abstained despite\n+  serialization-error/deployment/rollback evidence, and `inc-008` demanded\n+  additional downstream confirmation despite certificate evidence.\n+- Confidence values are model-assigned, uncalibrated and can remain high in\n+  inconclusive reports. Both approaches recovered the injected metrics failure with one tool retry; no transport retries occurred.\n\nConcrete failures included Critic referencing index 0 in an empty follow-up list, corrections that violated candidate/role preservation, and Reporting changing accepted hypotheses. No repairs or reruns were made.\n\n**Remaining limitations:** confidence remains uncalibrated; mechanisms can be mislabeled initiating causes, and hypothetical dependency issues still provoke over-abstention. Rubric credits are imperfect: baseline `inc-005` received credit without acquiring the configuration change, and `inc-008` recommended renewing the payments certificate rather than ledger's. Recommendations were text only, never executed, and are not safety-validated. One run per case establishes neither repeatability nor statistical superiority; the other nine are not an independent external holdout.\n\nEverything is saved in **`outputs\\benchmark-final\\`**, including raw responses, all reports/traces, JSON/CSV results, both cohort summaries, cost reconciliation and detailed manual findings. Event ID: `8aa244f1-cb36-4bca-b57b-cadd806c17f0`

**The approved benchmark finished: 20 live investigations, no repeats. Baseline performed better on this batch, but both systems showed substantial reliability limitations.** Investigator code, prompts, model/settings, dataset, rubric and previous results remained unchanged; all **156 protected files** were verified.

### Accuracy and execution

Failures and abstentions on answerable cases remain in the accuracy denominator. **`inc-009` is intentionally inconclusive** and is scored separately.

| Cohort | Approach | Answerable accuracy | Terminal failures | Limited support precision |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| All ten | Multi-agent | 0/9 — 0% | 7/10 | 30/55 — 54.5% |
| All ten | Baseline | 3/9 — 33.3% | 4/10 | 9/24 — 37.5% |
| Other nine, excluding `inc-001` | Multi-agent | 0/8 — 0% | 6/9 | 30/55 — 54.5% |
| Other nine, excluding `inc-001` | Baseline | 3/8 — 37.5% | 4/9 | 7/21 — 33.3% |

“Correct” below means credited by the unchanged limited rubric—not a fully verified causal explanation.

| Incident | Multi-agent | Baseline |
|---|---|---|
| `inc-001` | Reasoning failure | Ranked, incorrect |
| `inc-002` | Completed, inconclusive | Ranked, rubric-correct |
| `inc-003` | Critic failure | Analysis failure |
| `inc-004` | Critic failure | Ranked, incorrect |
| `inc-005` | Critic correction failure | Ranked, rubric-correct |
| `inc-006` | Critic correction failure | Analysis failure |
| `inc-007` | Reporting failure | Ranked, incorrect; tool failure recovered |
| `inc-008` | Completed, inconclusive | Ranked, rubric-correct |
| `inc-009` | Completed, appropriately inconclusive | Analysis failure |
| `inc-010` | Critic and Reporting failures | Analysis failure |

Multi-agent’s seven failed inconclusive outputs are **failure fallbacks**, not successful abstentions. Baseline’s failure fallback on `inc-009` does **not** count as appropriate inconclusiveness.

### Citation validity versus support

Every emitted citation existed and was acquired: **60/60** multi-agent and **24/24** baseline; excluding `inc-001`, **60/60** and **21/21**. One multi-agent and four baseline reports contained no citations.

The support scores above measure limited fact/witness relationships separately. Contradiction-link matches were **2/5** for multi-agent and **n/a** for baseline. Empty reports contribute no citations; retained hypotheses in failed reports still contribute to grounding scores. Citation validity is therefore not evidence of successful diagnosis.

### Resources and cost

Means include unsuccessful investigations. Token totals are actual provider-reported usage, including rejected responses and corrections.

| Cohort / approach | Tools / model requests | Mean latency | Input / output tokens | Calculated cost |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| All ten / multi-agent | 59 / 94 | 32.50 s | 313,194 / 38,777 | $0.1873208 |
| All ten / baseline | 62 / 44 | 13.35 s | 185,604 / 15,661 | $0.0992992 |
| Other nine / multi-agent | 54 / 88 | 33.83 s | 293,082 / 36,314 | $0.1753352 |

No systemic authentication/billing failure or tool/request/token/time budget exhaustion occurred. Three completed multi-agent investigations reached the **two-follow-up-round ceiling** and remained inconclusive.

Recommendations were advisory only, never executed or safety-validated.

Transient operations have three total attempts, selected output\n+errors get at most one correction, and feedback is limited to two rounds.\n+Conservative input/schema reservations are replaced by provider usage; unknown\n+usage remains explicitly reserved.\n+\n+The frozen benchmark ran twenty live investigations, one per approach on ten\n+synthetic cases. Multi-agent scored 0/9 answerable-case rubric accuracy with seven\n+terminal failures; baseline scored 3/9 with four. Excluding development case\n+inc-001 gives 0/8 versus 3/8. Total measured consumption was 498,798 input and 54,438 output\n+tokens, costing USD 0.2866200 at published rates, with no cached input.\n+\n+These results do not demonstrate multi-agent superiority. More model roles\n+created additional validation failure points and excessive caution. Baseline\n+was cheaper and more accurate under the rubric, but often stopped at mechanisms.\n+All emitted citations existed; limited support precision was 54.5% versus 37.5%.\n+The evaluator recognizes enumerated facts/witness relationships, not general\n+semantic entailment. Some rubric credits omit the initiating change or correct\n+service attribution. Confidence is uncalibrated; uncertainty classifications\n+remain model-dependent. Advisory recommendations can be unsafe or misdirected\n+and were never executed.\n+\n+Offline tests establish scheduling and contract behavior, not reliable live\n+diagnosis. One run per case cannot establish repeatability or statistical\n+superiority; the synthetic corpus is not an external holdout. Isolation is\n+loader/tool/prompt separation, not an OS sandbox, and the provider model is\n+deprecated.
